proposals.before: Li Sizhao, whose courtesy name was Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, military commissioner of Dai and younger brother of the Martial Emperor's mother.
proposals.after: Li Sizhao, whose courtesy name was Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, prefect of Dai and younger full brother of the Martial Emperor.
proposals.reason: 母弟 means a younger brother by the same mother, not the mother's brother; 刺史 is prefect, not military commissioner.

proposals.before: In the fourth year he was made commander of the inner guard, returned to aid Hezhong, routed Bian forces at Hubi Fort, captured the Bian general Hua Li, and was promoted to acting Grand Mentor for his service.
proposals.after: In the fourth year he was made commander of the inner guard, returned to aid Hezhong, routed Bian forces at Hubi Fort, captured the Bian general Hua Li, and was promoted to acting Pushe for his service.
proposals.reason: 檢校僕射 is acting Pushe (Vice Director), not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: In Guanghua 3 the Bian attacked Cangzhou. Liu Rengong appealed for help, and Sizhao was sent through Xing and Mo to relieve him.
proposals.after: In Guanghua 3 the Bian attacked Cangzhou. Liu Rengong appealed for help, and Sizhao was sent through Xing and Ming to relieve him.

proposals.before: He then attacked and captured Mo Prefecture, taking its commander Zhu Shaozong prisoner.
proposals.after: He then attacked and captured Ming Prefecture, taking its commander Zhu Shaozong prisoner.
proposals.reason: 洺州 is Ming Prefecture, not Mo Prefecture.

proposals.before: In the ninth month the Liang founder led thirty thousand men in person to Linmo, while Ge Congzhou laid an ambush at Qingshan Pass.
proposals.after: In the ninth month the Liang founder led thirty thousand men in person to Linming, while Ge Congzhou laid an ambush at Qingshan Pass.
proposals.reason: 臨洺 is Linming, not Linmo.

proposals.before: The Martial Emperor was about to follow this advice; Sizhao urgently argued that it must not be done. Still undecided, he was saved when Grand Consort Liu spoke forcefully within, and the Martial Emperor then stopped.
proposals.after: The Martial Emperor was about to follow this advice; Sizhao urgently argued that it must not be done. Still undecided, he relied on Grand Consort Liu speaking forcefully from within, and afterwards he stopped.
proposals.reason: 武後且止 means the Martial Emperor afterwards stopped; 賴 is 'relied on', not 'was saved'.

proposals.before: Sizhao governed Ze and Lu, holding offices from Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian up to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Sizhao governed Ze and Lu, holding offices from Minister of Education (Situ) and Grand Guardian up to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister of Education / Grand Preceptor of the Masses, not Grand Preceptor (太師), which appears only in the next sentence as a posthumous gift.

proposals.before: You are marked as a rebel. What face do you have left to show the world!
proposals.after: You bear the name of rebel. With what face can you appear again before the realm!
proposals.reason: 何麵更見天下 uses 麵 for 面; the sense is 'with what face can you see the world again'.

proposals.before: When the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, he served under Zhou Dewei at Yuyu. Siben led cavalry in daily skirmishes with the Bian, presented more than a thousand captives in all, and was made military commissioner of Dai.
proposals.after: When the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, he served under Zhou Dewei at Yuyu. Siben led cavalry in daily skirmishes with the Bian, presented more than a thousand captives in all, and was made prefect of Dai.
proposals.reason: 代州刺史 is prefect of Dai, not military commissioner.

proposals.before: At the battle of Shen he was rewarded with the post of military commissioner of Dai and overall commander of troops north of Shiling Pass, and was later promoted to military commissioner of Zhenwu.
proposals.after: At the battle of Shen he was rewarded with the post of prefect of Dai and overall commander of troops north of Shiling Pass, and was later promoted to military commissioner of Zhenwu.

proposals.after: Early in the Tiancheng era Emperor Mingzong, mindful of old service, posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 明宗 is Emperor Mingzong; 詔贈太尉 is a posthumous honorary appointment, not an enfeoffment.

decisions.reason: 賴 introduces Grand Consort Liu as the reason the proposal was abandoned; 武皇 is the subject who finally desisted. This preserves that logic in natural English.
